title: Crispy Baked Tortilla Pizza That Bakes in Under 10 Minutes
description: Make a crispy baked tortilla pizza in under 10 minutes with this foolproof recipe. Perfect for busy weeknights, movie nights, and fast family dinners.
storyHeading: Why Everyone Asks for This Recipe
story: When weeknight fatigue hits hard around 6 PM, this crispy baked tortilla pizza saves dinner at my house every single time. My teenagers used to complain about store-bought frozen options until I started making these on large flour tortillas. During recipe testing, I learned the hard way that piling too much sauce makes the base soggy; now, I brush a very thin layer of marinara right to the edges so the tortilla fries up golden and crisp in the hot oven. It feeds a hungry crowd in minutes, and you can easily scale up the ingredient station so everyone builds their own custom slice.
ingredients: 1/2 cup marinara sauce or pizza sauce
1/2 cup sliced pepperoni or cooked crumbled Italian sausage
1 tbsp extra virgin olive oil for brushing edges
1 tsp dried oregano or Italian seasoning
instructions: Preheat your oven to 425°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper to ensure the bottom of the tortillas get extra crispy without burning.
Place the tortillas flat on the prepared baking sheet and lightly brush the exposed edges with extra virgin olive oil.
Spoon about two tablespoons of marinara sauce onto the center of each tortilla and spread it out evenly, leaving a small border for the crust.
Sprinkle the shredded mozzarella evenly over the sauce, top with your favorite meats or veggies, and finish with a dusting of Parmesan and Italian seasoning.
Bake on the middle rack for 6 to 8 minutes until the cheese is bubbling, golden brown around the edges, and the tortilla bottoms are crisp enough to hold a slice without drooping.
proHack: Slide the baking sheet onto the lowest rack for the final 60 seconds of cooking if your crust needs extra crunch.
servingIdea: Serve alongside a big bowl of chopped Caesar salad tossed with garlic croutons and a side of warm garlic knots.
storage: Store leftover baked slices in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. Reheat directly in a 400°F oven or toaster oven for 3 minutes to restore the crispy crust.

faqs.question: Can I use corn tortillas instead of flour?
faqs.answer: Flour tortillas work best because they hold up under the weight of the sauce and cheese and crisp evenly, whereas standard corn tortillas tend to crack and dry out too quickly in a hot oven.

faqs.question: How do I prevent the center of the pizza from getting soggy?
faqs.answer: Keep your sauce layer thin and avoid watery toppings like fresh sliced tomatoes unless you blot them dry with a paper towel beforehand.

faqs.question: Can I make these ahead for a kids' party?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can set up a DIY topping station with bowls of cheese, pepperoni, and bell peppers, allowing guests to assemble their own tortillas right before popping them onto hot baking sheets.
